transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Hello, Ms. Brightwater, I'm Dr. Lindqvist. Your primary care office sent you for numbness in your hands. Tell me about it.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: For about four months my right hand goes numb, mostly the thumb, index and middle fingers. It wakes me up at night and I shake my hand to get the feeling back.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Is the left hand involved at all?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: A little in the last month, but the right is much worse. I'm right-handed.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any neck pain, weakness, or dropping things?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No neck pain. I do drop my keys sometimes. My grip feels weaker.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: What kind of work do you do?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I'm a dental hygienist, so I'm using small instruments with my hands all day.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any other medical problems?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: High cholesterol. I take atorvastatin 20 mg every night. And I had my gallbladder out years ago.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Do you smoke?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, I don't smoke.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Any family history of nerve problems?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My mother had thyroid problems. Nothing with nerves that I know of. Oh, about smoking, I should be honest, I still have a few cigarettes on weekends.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Thanks for telling me. Any balance problems, numbness in your feet, or bowel or bladder changes?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: No, none of that.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: On exam, Tinel's sign is positive at the right wrist and Phalen's test is positive on the right after twenty seconds. There's mild weakness of right thumb abduction, 4 out of 5, and mild atrophy at the base of the right thumb. Sensation is reduced in the right thumb, index and middle fingers. Left hand strength is normal. Reflexes are 2 and symmetric, and neck range of motion is full.

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: This looks like carpal tunnel syndrome, right worse than left. Because there's weakness and some atrophy, I'd like a nerve conduction study and EMG of both arms. In the meantime, wear a wrist splint at night on the right, in a neutral position.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Okay. Can I keep working?

transcript.speaker: clinician
transcript.text: Yes. Take short breaks to rest your hands. I'd also encourage you to quit smoking completely; we can help with that. We'll follow up after the nerve study, in about four weeks.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Sounds good.

sections.title: Chief complaint
sections.text: Numbness in the hands, right worse than left, for four months.

sections.title: History of present illness
sections.text: 52-year-old right-handed woman with four months of numbness of the right thumb, index and middle fingers that wakes her at night; she shakes her hand to get the feeling back. The left hand is involved a little in the last month. Grip feels weaker and she drops her keys sometimes. No neck pain.

sections.title: Past medical history
sections.text: High cholesterol, on atorvastatin 20 mg every night. Gallbladder removed years ago.

sections.title: Family history
sections.text: Mother had thyroid problems. No known family history of nerve problems.

sections.title: Social history
sections.text: Dental hygienist, using small instruments with her hands all day. Smokes a few cigarettes on weekends.

sections.title: Review of systems
sections.text: No balance problems, no numbness in the feet, no bowel or bladder changes.

sections.title: Physical exam
sections.text: Tinel's sign positive at the right wrist. Phalen's test positive on the right after twenty seconds. Right thumb abduction 4/5 with mild atrophy at the base of the right thumb. Sensation reduced in the right thumb, index and middle fingers. Left hand strength normal. Reflexes 2 and symmetric. Neck range of motion full.

sections.title: Assessment and plan
sections.text: Carpal tunnel syndrome, right worse than left, with weakness and mild atrophy. Nerve conduction study and EMG of both arms. Wrist splint at night on the right, in a neutral position. Short breaks to rest the hands at work. Encouraged to quit smoking. Follow-up after the nerve study, in about four weeks.

sections.title: Patient instructions
sections.text: Wear the wrist splint on your right wrist at night, in a neutral position. Take short breaks to rest your hands at work. We will schedule a nerve conduction study and EMG. Quitting smoking completely helps; we can help with that. Return in about four weeks, after the nerve study.

mustNotInvent.description: No medication for nerve pain was discussed.
No injection or surgery was discussed.
